title: Data Analyst
tagline: Answer business questions with SQL, spreadsheets and clear dashboards.
about: Data analysts help organisations understand what's happening and why. You'll query databases, build dashboards, investigate metric changes and present findings to decision-makers.
It's one of the most accessible entry points into tech: less programming than other paths, lots of business impact, and a natural stepping stone to data science or analytics engineering.
day: Write SQL to answer business questions

phases.title: Spreadsheets & thinking with data
phases.goal: Analyse data in the tool every business already uses.

nodes.d: Join and summarise data without code.
Mean, median, spread and distributions: summarise honestly.
links: Seeing Theory: visual probability and statistics

nodes.d: Turn a vague request into a specific, answerable question with a metric.

project.d: Analyse a public sales dataset in a spreadsheet: pivot tables, a few charts, and a one-page summary of what's driving revenue.

phases.title: SQL
phases.goal: Query databases directly; the analyst's core skill.

nodes.d: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, aggregates and GROUP BY.
Combine tables correctly, and spot when a join duplicates rows.
Time-based analysis: retention cohorts and funnels.

project.d: Answer ten business questions about an e-commerce dataset with SQL, including a retention cohort and a funnel, and document each query.

phases.title: Visualisation & BI
phases.goal: Turn numbers into dashboards people use.

nodes.d: Pick the right chart, remove clutter, highlight the point.
Build interactive dashboards on live data.
Dashboards that answer questions at a glance.
pandas for data too big or messy for spreadsheets.
Know when a difference is real.

project.d: An end-to-end analysis of a real dataset: SQL extraction, Python cleaning, a published dashboard and a short memo with recommendations.

interview: SQL live test (joins, aggregates, window functions).

Dashboard critique or a take-home dashboard.
